concepts.def: The first patriarch, called by God to leave his homeland for Canaan and given the covenant promising land and countless descendants.
Circumcision, commanded in Genesis 17 as the lasting sign of the covenant between God and Abraham's descendants.
The binding of Isaac in Genesis 22, when Abraham's willingness to obey God became the supreme test and proof of his faith.
The covenant passed to Abraham's son Isaac and grandson Jacob, who was renamed Israel and whose twelve sons fathered the twelve tribes.
Sold into Egypt by his brothers, Joseph rose to power by interpreting Pharaoh's dreams and brought Jacob's family to settle in Egypt.
Called at the burning bush, Moses led the Israelites out of slavery in Egypt and received the Torah, including the Ten Commandments, at Mount Sinai.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Judaism: The Patriarchs & Early Leaders — a core area of GCSE Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Judaism: The Patriarchs & Early Leaders brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Judaism: The Patriarchs & Early Leaders.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What was the sign of God's covenant with Abraham?
options: Circumcision (brit milah)
The rainbow
Lighting Sabbath candles
The Passover meal

mcqs.q: Which patriarch was given the new name 'Israel'?
options: Jacob
Abraham
Isaac
Joseph

mcqs.q: How was Moses called by God to lead the Israelites?
options: Through the burning bush
In a dream about seven cows
By a voice from the Ark
Through a prophet at the Temple
The Israelites' deliverance from slavery in Egypt
The giving of the Ten Commandments
The creation of the world
The rededication of the Temple

mcqs.q: Did Abraham follow the Torah's laws as Jews do today?
options: No - Abraham lived long before the Torah was given at Sinai; tradition honours him as the first to turn from idolatry to one God and as father of the covenant people.
The covenant was an agreement between Abraham and Pharaoh.
Abraham was a king who ruled from Jerusalem.
Abraham kept kosher laws and festivals exactly like modern Jews.

mcqs.q: Did Moses lead the people into the Promised Land?
options: Moses personally led the conquest and settlement of Canaan.
The covenant was an agreement between Abraham and Pharaoh.
Moses sailed the people to Canaan by ship.
No - according to the Torah, Moses saw the land from Mount Nebo but died before entering it; Joshua led the Israelites across the Jordan.

mcqs.q: Is the covenant just a one-sided promise from God?
options: Abraham was a king who ruled from Jerusalem.
The covenant only involves God giving and Israel receiving.
No - the covenant is a two-way bond: God's promises of land and descendants come with obligations, such as circumcision for Abraham and Torah observance at Sinai.
The covenant was an agreement between Abraham and Pharaoh.
